source_text: Ὁ μὲν οὖν θεῖος νόμος οὐ μόνον κωλύει τὸ εἰδώλοις προσκυνεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχείοις, ἡλίῳ σελήνῃ ἢ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἄστροις, ἀλλ᾿ οὔτε τῷ οὐρανῷ οὔτε γῇ οὔτε θαλάσσῃ ἢ πηγαῖς ἢ ποταμοῖς θρησκεύειν· ἀλλ᾿ ἢ μόνῳ τῷ ὄντως θεῷ καὶ ποιητῇ τῶν ὅλων χρὴ λατρεύειν ἐν ὁσιότητι καρδίας καὶ εἰλικρινεῖ γνώμῃ.
pass_a_gloss: The divine law indeed not only forbids to worship idols, but also the elements, the sun, the moon, or the other stars, nor to worship the heaven, nor the earth, nor the sea, nor the springs, nor the rivers; but it is necessary to worship only the one who is truly God and the maker of all things in holiness of heart and with a pure intention.
pass_b_english: The divine law forbids not only the worship of idols but also the worship of the elements — the sun, the moon, or the other stars — and it forbids worship of heaven, earth, sea, springs, or rivers. Instead, one must worship only the one who is truly God and the maker of all things, doing so with a holy heart and a pure intention.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the prohibitions and the positive command of the Greek text. Pass A preserves the structure and nuances of the Greek clauses, including the 'not only... but also' and the series of negations. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the semantic integrity of the source.
